projects.name: Project Meridian
canonical_bullets: Designed a production-shaped RAG architecture -- versioned document ingestion, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + HNSW vector search with RRF fusion), and cross-encoder reranking -- over a 40k-article internal support-documentation corpus with routine content updates.

Built a quantitative evaluation harness (Recall@k, nDCG@k, MRR, LLM-judged faithfulness/correctness) that gates index promotion via alias-based blue/green deployment, then used it to validate a cost/latency optimization pass: 24% cheaper, 33% faster, with Recall@10 within 2 points of baseline (0.68 -> 0.66).
Added prompt-injection, scope, and PII guardrails with citation validation, blocking ~78% of a curated adversarial evaluation set; served via FastAPI + Redis at ~900 ms p50 end-to-end latency.
alternate_facts_for_dynamic_tailoring: Corpus: internal support-documentation articles, refreshed on a rolling basis
Addresses document sections via standardized section codes rather than pattern matching
Separates permanent document identity, versions, and derived chunks so retrieval units rebuild without losing history
Agent control flow: retrieve, grade, generate, bounded query-rewrite, refusal paths; near-duplicate collapse, diversity control, token-aware context packing
Maintains versioned indexes and rollback-oriented operations

projects.name: Project Nova
canonical_bullets: Designed an end-to-end course-recommendation engine over an 8K-course catalog using hybrid dense+sparse retrieval (ChromaDB + BM25 with RRF) and a fine-tuned cross-encoder reranker, improving Recall@20 from 0.52 -> 0.64 and nDCG@10 to 0.68.

Built a self-distillation pipeline with LLM-as-judge to generate ~5K training pairs at near-zero cost, then fine-tuned a small open-weight cross-encoder (QLoRA) and bi-encoder; added LLM-powered tag enrichment and engagement-weighted personalization via LangGraph.

Optimized for production with ONNX/int8 export, two-tier Redis caching, and HyDE expansion -- reducing average latency to ~140 ms and LLM cost by ~30% -- then deployed as a multi-container FastAPI service.
alternate_facts_for_dynamic_tailoring: Structured course metadata with LLM-based tag enrichment for sparse entries; controlled tag vocabulary and provenance flags
Selective HyDE expansion used only for short/vague requests
LangGraph nodes for query parsing, hybrid search, reranking, and explanation generation
Engagement-weighted preference vector; query blending, enrolled-course filtering, catalog-grounded explanations

projects.name: Project Vertex
projects.status: Team project (two people: Candidate Example, Teammate Example); course context
bullets: Co-developed a volunteer-opportunity matching platform covering more than 400 local nonprofit listings by combining a learned fit-scoring model, geographic filtering, and applicant-tracking workflows.
Built the listing-history and match-replay APIs to evaluate fit-scoring signals over time and separate retrospective analysis from forward-looking validation.
Developed volunteer-comparison, application-tracking, authentication, and match-history workflows across a Next.js, FastAPI, Supabase/PostgreSQL, pgvector, and XGBoost stack.
cautions: Unverified early scoring-weight drafts exist in the project record -- do not present as final unless reconfirmed.

projects.name: Project Cascade
scope_facts: Predicts next-term course-enrollment demand from time-ordered scheduling and historical attendance data
Compares six classifiers with four scheduling-heuristic baselines using held-out and expanding-window validation (not random cross-validation)
XGBoost is the strongest reported model; SHAP used for feature attribution
Includes leakage checks, conformal-prediction uncertainty estimates, and capacity-constraint sensitivity analysis
Exposes results through a FastAPI backend and React interface
bullets: Benchmarked six machine-learning classifiers against four scheduling-heuristic baselines for next-term course-enrollment demand by using point-in-time features and time-ordered validation.
Achieved a 0.61 held-out ROC-AUC with XGBoost and a 0.59 mean ROC-AUC across 12 expanding-window terms.
Improved result interpretability and evaluation discipline by combining SHAP attribution, leakage tests, conformal uncertainty estimates, and capacity-constraint sensitivity analysis.
Served screening and comparison results through a FastAPI backend and React interface.

projects.name: Project Horizon
bullets: Built a time-series demand-forecasting model for a simulated regional logistics network, reducing forecast error (MAPE) from 19% to 11% versus a naive seasonal baseline.
Packaged the forecasting model behind a weekly batch-scoring script that regenerated demand forecasts across 12 simulated distribution regions.
Containerized the scoring script with Docker so forecasts could be regenerated consistently on any schedule.
cautions: Use the 19%->11% MAPE figures (latest supplied values); older drafts citing different numbers are stale -- verify before submission.
